# SasaVenos Recommends Planche Sets Before Iron Cross To Protect Elbows

SasaVenos recommends doing planche sets first and then Iron Cross because planche is less demanding for the elbow and more technical, while Iron Cross is harder on the elbows. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]

## Details

- Doing planche right after Iron Cross is hard on the elbows. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]
- Planche sets are less demanding for the elbow and are more technical. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]
- Doing planche first means your elbows will still be fresh for Iron Cross, and you do not have to think about protraction, posterior pelvic tilt, having a good line and all the details needed for a planche. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]

## Evidence

- vid-BBuB0XMVhDw (SasaVenos): "If you do your planches right after the Iron Cross, your elbows probably aren't gonna like that, honestly."
- vid-BBuB0XMVhDw (SasaVenos): "A much better idea would be to do your planche sets first, which are less demanding for the elbow and are more technical anyway, and then the Iron Cross because your elbows will still be fresh"
- vid-BBuB0XMVhDw (SasaVenos): "and you don't have to think about protraction, posterior pelvic tilt, having a good line and all of these details that we do for a planche."
